neighbours.label: ' out' in a verb meaning to set forth or explain (lays out, sets out, spells out), on a broad pole
fire: In her new book, Hart lays out a bold plan for reform.
The report sets out a clear case against the merger.
The author spells out the risks of the new policy.
Chapter two lays out the evidence in great detail.
Lawyers mapped out their whole argument for the jury.
This short memo lays out how the system should work.
The minister set out the reasons for the decision.
Sanders laid out a sweeping vision in his speech.
quiet: In her new book, Hart walks out on a bad marriage.
The report came out a week after the merger.
The author ran out of paper for the new novel.
Chapter two was left out of the final edition.
Lawyers went out for dinner after the jury.
This short memo went out to all of the staff.
The minister stepped out for a moment before the decision.
Sanders passed out shortly after his speech.
